newsitem.title: USA: Viacom debt up, other U.S. corporate bonds flat.
newsitem.headline: Viacom debt up, other U.S. corporate bonds flat.

text.p: Investors in the U.S. investment-grade corporate bond market on Friday continued to focus on media and cable credits such as Viacom Inc and Tele-Communications Inc, with spreads in the broader market remaining unchanged.

Traders reported that the bid across the high-yield sector firmed slightly after experiencing weakness earlier in the day and week. Junk prices generally remained unchanged, although the casino and supermarket sectors experienced some softness.

Among investment-grade credits, spreads on Viacom 20-year bonds tightened by around 15 basis points after the company announced late in the day that it was dropping its settlement talks with Seagram Co. Ltd.'s MCA Inc.
Prices on Tele-Communications' bonds continued to decline following the release on Thursday of preliminary earnings, which were less than expected.
"The company has lost a lot of credibility with the investment community," said one trader.

In the high-yield sector, Trump Hotel & Casino Resorts 11 1/4 percent first mortgage notes due 2006 closed with a 95 1/2 bid, after trading as low as 94 earlier in the day. Casino America 12 1/2 senior secured notes of '03 closed at 102 1/2 after trading as low as 101 1/2, traders said.
Prices across the supermarket sector were off by 1/2 a point on average, a trader said.
On a more positive note for investors, Hlton Hotels Corp made a cash offer to purchase about $1 billion in debt of Bally's Grand Inc. at a premium.
"Bonds were expecting a higer tender price, but fundamentally it's still a positive because they will tender for them at a premium," said one trader.
He speculated that the bond holders may negotiate for an even higher price at a later date.

High-grade corporate issuance featured $250 million 10-year Baa2/BBB-plus rated notes from Las Vegas-based casino concern Mirage Resorts Inc via a Goldman Sachs & Co led syndicate. The notes were given a 7-1/4 percent coupon and priced at 99.869 to yield 7.268 percent or 73 basis points over the U.S. Treasury curve.
The Mirage issue was increased in size by $50 million.

Junk rated issues included a $125 million rule 144a private placement issue from Kelley Oil & Gas Corp via lead manager Morgan Stanley & Co Inc, sources said. The 10-year B3/B-minus rated senior subordinated notes were given a 10-3/8 percent coupon and priced at 99.75 to yield 10.41 percent or 388 basis points over Treasuries.
Elsewhere, Unifrax Corp issued $100 million B2/single-B rated senior notes due 2003 at par with a 10.50 percent coupon via a BT Securities Corp syndicate.
